title: Design System: Ball IQ — The Scouting Report

headline.purpose: The page's h1 only, two lines then straight into the question.

verdict-number.purpose: The single largest object on the page; appears only after the last question, coloured by the six-step verdict ramp.

verdict-tier.purpose: The tier word (Cone → Ballon d'Or); sized to out-rank every section heading.

section.purpose: Every h2 signpost; kept under the verdict tier's size deliberately.

lede.purpose: The one line under the headline.

sub.purpose: The paragraph under a section heading.

body.purpose: Base size: prose, answer options, table data.

sec.purpose: Supporting text: keys, colophon-style footer, Footle labels.

label.purpose: The one uppercase micro-label treatment, shared by five call-sites.

shadows.name: report-sheet
shadows.purpose: The primary paper object's shadow, plus an inset highlight simulating a lit sheet edge.

shadows.name: backing-sheet
shadows.purpose: The second sheet under the report, visible at its rotated edges.

shadows.name: verdict-slip
shadows.purpose: Lighter and tighter than the report's shadow; a smaller object landing on an already-shadowed stack.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Verdict land animation and stub bar fill easing.

motion.name: verdict-land
motion.value: land .5s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both — rotate(2.6deg) scale(1.045) opacity:0 to rotate(.7deg) scale(1) opacity:1
motion.purpose: Plays once when the verdict is revealed; fully suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: footle-shake
motion.purpose: Plays on an invalid Footle submission (wrong letter count).

components.name: Button — Primary
components.description: The single button shape on the page: ink-filled, used for verdict CTAs and any control living on paper.

components.name: Button — Alt
components.description: Ink-bordered, transparent-fill secondary action; inverts to the primary fill on hover.

components.name: Get App CTA
components.description: The masthead's single store-distribution affordance: paper-filled on the dark desk ground, the highest-contrast object in the bar.

components.name: Answer Option
components.description: A bordered newsprint answer button with a boxed letter chip; shown here in its four states (default, hit, miss, dim) as one reference block.

components.name: The Paper Sheet
components.description: Signature component. The oversized, rotated, double-shadowed newsprint report sitting on the dark desk — the page's central metaphor.

components.name: Verdict Stamp
components.description: Signature component. A second paper slip landing on the report once all five questions are answered; states the grade as number, word, and colour at once.

components.name: Running Report Row
components.description: One ledger row: discipline label, fill-only-on-correct progress bar, tabular outcome cell.
components.html: Premier League1 of 1

components.name: Footle Tile
components.description: One square of the Footle board in its three scored states plus the unplayed default.
components.html: AHAZ

narrative.overview:
The page is not about a football test; the page IS the test, and it files a report on the person taking it. It rejects the category's stock furniture on sight — no dark hero with a phone mockup floating in it, no three-card feature triptych, no counted stat printed as if size were the pitch. In its place: a near-black desk, grained like paper under raking light, with the scouting report itself lying on top of it as a physical, oversized sheet — wider than its own column, tilted a fraction of a degree, backed by a second sheet, casting a real double shadow. The report is not a card that happens to hold a quiz; the quiz is the report, and it fills itself in, in front of the reader, as they answer.

Everything that is not the report is desk: dark, quiet, near-monochrome, and flat. Everything that is the report is paper: ink on newsprint, ruled like a table, printed rather than glowing. The only place either surface is allowed a second colour is the one place a scout actually grades something, and that colour is always the same scout's ramp — oxblood through amber to green — never a decorative accent borrowed for anything else. Action itself is never a fourth hue: a button is filled with whichever of ink or newsprint is NOT the ground it sits on.

This was built by resonance-assignment (seed key cf2f8891, candidate 4 of 7), not by open-ended taste, and its own direction contract is the closest thing to a spec this world has. It explicitly rejects home-final.html, an earlier all-dark, no-paper direction kept in the same folder as an anti-reference.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds, not one: a dark desk (the world) and a lit paper sheet (the report), and every token belongs to exactly one of them.
One saturated family in the whole system — the scout's ramp — appearing only where something is actually being graded.
Zero border-radius anywhere in the file. Every edge is a hard corner; the only curves are the paper's own slight rotation.
Motion exists only as feedback tied to the reader's own action — never ambient, never on load, never decorative.
Contrast is measured, not assumed: several rules in the CSS carry the exact ratio a prior attempt failed and the ratio the shipped version clears.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: The only saturated colours anywhere in the system are the scout's ramp and its verdict variant. Nothing else is allowed a hue that isn't ink, paper, or desk.

rules.name: The Same-Weight Rule Rule
rules.body: hairline-rule and control-rule are the same visual weight but different jobs: one is furniture, the other is a control boundary held to a harder contrast floor.

rules.name: The Five-Plus-One Rule
rules.body: Five body-scale sizes carry every prose job; the uppercase micro-label is a distinct treatment (case + tracking), not a sixth size.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number a reader might compare against another number is set with tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Light-on-Dark Compensation Rule
rules.body: Text on the desk gets a touch more letter-spacing than the equivalent prose on paper; dark-on-light does not get the same bump.

rules.name: The Object Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow only appears where something is meant to read as a physical sheet resting on the desk — never for hover feedback, a generic card, or ambient atmosphere.

dos: Do keep the scout's ramp (oxblood → amber → green) as the only saturated colour family anywhere in the system.
Do fill a button with whichever of ink or newsprint is not the ground it sits on.
Do recede a de-emphasized state with a darker solid colour, never with opacity.
Do reserve shadow for the two paper objects (the report, the verdict); everything else on the desk stays flat.
Do guard every hover-only affordance with @media (hover:hover).
Do move focus explicitly whenever a click removes the element that held it.
donts: Don't introduce a fourth colour family for any reason.
Don't assume the three-step Scout's Ramp and the six-step Verdict Ramp are the same scale re-sampled.
Don't add motion that isn't a direct response to the reader's own action.
Don't collapse the Masthead CTA, the Letterhead, and the Footer distribution line into one component.
